common_name: Vertigo Deep Blue Torenia (Compact Non-Fading Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Start seed indoors on the soil surface without covering, since germination is light-enhanced; move transplants out after all frost danger has passed into a bed with consistent moisture.

directions: Vertigo Deep Blue is a compact, mounding wishbone flower bred for saturated violet-blue blooms that resist the fading common in older torenia strains through summer heat. Sow seed on the surface of moist, sterile starting mix and hold at 72-77F, since seed needs light rather than soil covering to germinate. Set transplants into humus-rich, evenly moist beds or containers in dappled to full shade, where the tidy, self-branching habit keeps performing without deadheading through the hottest, most humid stretch of summer. Because the mounded form holds its shape rather than trailing, it pairs well with upright shade perennials in mixed plantings.

common_name: Hi-Lite Mix Torenia (Bicolor and Tricolor Wishbone Flower Blend)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and transplant into shade beds or containers once nights stay reliably above 50F.

directions: Hi-Lite Mix produces an unusually dense mix of bicolor and tricolor blooms in white, pink, magenta, and blue on a single tight, mounded plant, rather than segregating colors into separate lots. Grow in rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in shade to dappled light, where the glossy compact foliage stays full without stretching or flopping. The abundant 1-2 inch flowers are self-cleaning and multi-branched stems keep producing new buds through summer heat without a need for deadheading. Its tight, uniform habit makes it well suited to container edges and mass shade bedding where a single-color block isn't the goal.

common_name: Summery Love Pure White Torenia (AAS-Winning Compact Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Set out transplants from late spring through early summer; an All-America Selections winner recognized for holding clean white color and vigor through long, wet, humid stretches.

directions: Summery Love Pure White was named an All-America Selections winner for clean, yellow-throat-free white flowers held more densely than on older torenia lines, on a compact, well-branched plant that needs no staking or deadheading. Unlike most wishbone flower cultivars bred strictly for shade, this AAS trial performer holds up in both full sun and shade, making it more flexible for mixed borders and container plantings that get variable light. Keep soil rich and consistently moist but never waterlogged, and expect nonstop bloom from late spring through the first frost. Its dense branching and durability held up through judges' trial seasons marked by long, hot, wet, and humid conditions that stress most shade annuals.
